consensus_summary: Worship is exclusive reverent adoration, homage, and self-surrender to God alone (ascribing supreme worth), expressed in bodily bowing/prostration and whole-life orientation/submission; common alternatives cover liturgy, sacrifice of praise, lifestyle service, and experiential encounter, while pure reduction to music/singing is widely noted but criticized.
book_summary: Worship is to bow down and serve: homage in the body plus allegiance in the life, the fear of the LORD made visible, kept at His appointed times on His terms; it is explicitly not the song service, as Scripture separates worship from singing.
consensus_core_identification: exclusive reverent homage/self-surrender to God (bodily bowing + life orientation/ascription of worth)
book_core_identification: bow down and serve (bodily homage + life allegiance); fear of the LORD made visible at appointed times on His terms (not singing)
boundary_disagreement: Book requires appointed times/God's terms and reclassifies song service as non-worship (separated in Scripture); consensus is broader on continuous lifestyle, varied liturgical forms, and praise without mandating those temporal/conditional strictures (while already often rejecting music-alone reduction).
material_contradiction: None on the shared core of exclusive bowing/serving homage to God; disagreement is boundary/extension only.
rationale: Minimum cores both center on bowing down and serving God with bodily homage and life allegiance. Book preserves that referent but materially narrows precision and cases via appointed-times condition, 'on His terms,' and explicit exclusion of song service (supported by the 2 Chr separation scene), yielding refinement rather than equivalence or replacement.
strongest_objection: Could be scored MATCH if appointed times and anti-song emphasis are treated as immaterial detail already latent in consensus critiques of music reduction and bowing language.
